title: CERN, the European particle physics laboratory, and French AI company Mistral have signed a statement of intent to build the first foundation model for collider physics.
key_facts: CERN and Mistral signed a statement of intent for a long-term partnership on foundation models for scientific discovery
Goal: a single pretrained Large Physics Model, first foundation model for collider physics
Trained on billions of simulated proton-proton collisions at the LHC
Tasks: reconstructing collisions, identifying particles, flagging unexpected signals, evaluating future detector designs
CERN holds about one exabyte of LHC data; collisions to rise tenfold with the HL-LHC around 2030
Quoted: Enrica Porcari (CERN Chief Information Officer) and Johannes Brandstetter (Mistral VP of AI for Engineering)
quote_evidence: CERN, the European Laboratory for Particle Physics, and Mistral, a European developer of large-scale AI models, have signed a statement of intent to establish a long-term strategic partnership focused on developing foundation models for scientific discovery.
At the heart of this work is the ambition to develop a single pretrained Large Physics Model – the first foundation model for collider physics.
CERN is home to one of the world's largest volumes of scientific data, with around one exabyte – one million terabytes – of experimental data from the LHC stored to date.
why_it_matters_hint: One shared model could replace a chain of specialised analysis steps.
